ORDER REASSIGNING CASE.IT IS ORDERED that this case is reassigned to the Honorable Eumi K. Lee in the San Jose Division for all further proceedings.1. All future filings shall bear the initials EKL immediately after the case number.2. All case management conference dates are vacated and will be reset by the Court.3. All hearing dates presently scheduled are VACATED. However, existing briefing schedules for motions remain unchanged. Motions must be RENOTICED for hearing before Judge Lee by the moving party for a date consistent with the Court’s law and motion calendar, but the renoticing of the hearing does not affect the prior briefing schedule.4. Deadlines for ADR compliance and discovery cutoffs remain unchanged.5. All pretrial conference and trial dates currently set for after December 4, 2024, and all other deadlines associated with the case, will remain in place unless otherwise ordered.6. All pretrial conference and trial dates scheduled on or before December 4, 2024, are vacated. Other pretrial deadlines (eg., motions in limine, pretrial statements, proposed joint trial exhibits, etc.) will remain in place. The Court will notify the parties when a status conference will be held to schedule a new pretrial conference and trial dates for affected cases.7. Matters currently referred to a Magistrate Judge will remain before that Magistrate Judge absent further notice.8. On or before September 16, 2024, the parties shall file a Joint Case Management Statement (separate statements are appropriate if either party is proceeding without counsel). The statement should not exceed ten pages in length and should address all issues outlines in the Standing Order for All Judges of the Northern District. the approved form for such statements can be accessed here: a. The parties are not required to complete a section if inapplicable. As number 20, the statement shall provide the following information: (i) a list or description of each party; (ii) a summary of all claims, counter-claims, cross-claims, or third party claims and the date the complaint and cross-complaint(s) were filed; and (iii) a brief procedural history of the case (chart format welcomed) including, but not limited to, any ADR proceedings or settlement conferences that have been scheduled or concluded and any appellate proceedings that are pending or concluded. b. If the parties believe that an immediate case management conference is needed, the parties shall explain why and identify the urgent matters that require attention. If there is no immediate need, a case management conference will be scheduled or reset pursuant to Paragraph 2 of this Order as needed. 9. coverage.headline: Anthropic seeks partial dismissal in music publishers' $3B lyrics suit – as CEO moves to drop the direct-infringement claim against him
coverage.summary: Anthropic has sought partial dismissal of the separate $3B 'Concord II' suit, arguing the publishers' second amended complaint covering roughly 21,000 works fails to cite a single example of an infringing Claude output. The filing provides context on the procedural posture of the original Concord I case (5:24-cv-03811), including the March 2026 partial summary judgment motion and upcoming October 21, 2026 hearing.

coverage.headline: Anthropic Seeks Partial Dismissal in 'Concord II' Copyright Lawsuit
coverage.summary: Anthropic has moved for partial dismissal of the 'Concord II' $3 billion lawsuit, including seeking to drop a direct copyright infringement claim against CEO Dario Amodei on grounds that no evidence of his direct infringement exists. The motion also targets the publishers' output-based infringement and DMCA claims.

coverage.headline: Anthropic Says Music Publishers Still Can't Show Copyright Infringement in US Case
coverage.summary: Anthropic moved to dismiss the amended U.S. copyright claims filed by Universal Music, Concord Music Group, and ABKCO, arguing the complaint lacks any example of an allegedly infringing output from its Claude AI.

coverage.headline: Music Publishers Expand Copyright Lawsuit Against Anthropic Over Song Lyrics
coverage.summary: Concord Music Group, Universal Music Publishing Group, and ABKCO filed an expanded complaint on July 22 in N.D. California, incorporating internal discovery records and alleging Claude was intentionally built to reproduce copyrighted lyrics—describing the capability as 'a feature, not a bug.' The amended complaint covers roughly 500 songs, while a separate 2026 suit involves more than 20,000 songs.

coverage.headline: Music publishers file amended lyrics lawsuit against Anthropic – just as AI firm's separate $1.5B piracy settlement with authors wins court approval
coverage.summary: Concord Music Group, Universal Music Publishing Group, and ABKCO filed a Second Amended Complaint on July 22 in N.D. California (case 5:24-cv-03811), an expanded version of their May amended complaint covering ~500 songs. The publishers have narrowed the case to direct infringement and alleged removal of copyright management information, and moved for partial summary judgment in March 2026.

coverage.headline: High-Stakes Direct Infringement Claims Take Center Stage in Dialed-Back Concord v. Anthropic Copyright Cases
coverage.summary: The Concord v. Anthropic cases have shed most of their contributory infringement claims, with direct infringement now taking center stage as the publishers filed their second amended complaint.

coverage.headline: Publishers Back Concord Music Group's AI Suit
coverage.summary: Four organizations—including the Association of American Publishers and the Authors Guild—filed an amicus brief supporting Concord Music Group's copyright suit against Anthropic, arguing the AI company's training practices are not transformative and interfere with legitimate licensing markets. The brief contends copyright law does not permit systematic copying of human-authored works without permission.

coverage.headline: RIAA, NMPA, and more file amicus brief backing UMG, Concord and ABKCO in original Anthropic case, arguing AI firm's unlicensed copying is 'inexcusable'
coverage.summary: The RIAA, NMPA, and allied groups filed amicus briefs in Concord I (5:24-cv-03811) supporting the publishers' partial summary judgment motion, characterizing Anthropic as a 'holdout' that has chosen to scrape copyrighted content rather than license it like competitors. The briefs cite academic research challenging AI firms' claims that training data is not memorized by models.

coverage.headline: Anthropic Beats Music Firms' Bid for Users' Personal Data
coverage.summary: A California federal judge denied music publishers' request for the personal data of Claude users who sought copyrighted lyrics, ruling the production of third-party user information was not necessary for the infringement litigation in Concord I (5:24-cv-03811). Publishers had argued the data was critical to identify users who received copyrighted lyric outputs that Anthropic did not preserve before the lawsuit.
